title: The Date-Stamped Backup
description: Produce an /etc/app backup whose filename contains today's date, as the retention policy requires.
scenario: The retention policy requires every config backup to be named etc-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz (today's real date) under /tmp/backups, so old backups sort chronologically and a rotation script can purge them. Yesterday's backup was named 'backup-final-final.tar.gz' and was rejected. Archive /etc/app with the date embedded via command substitution.
symptoms: No backup of /etc/app exists at all
The naming convention etc-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz is not negotiable — the rotation script globs it
mission: Create /tmp/backups/ and produce /tmp/backups/etc-$(date +%F).tar.gz containing the /etc/app configuration directory.

hints.title: date +%F
hints.content: `date +%F` prints the current date as YYYY-MM-DD — exactly the convention the rotation script expects.

hints.title: Command substitution
hints.content: `$(command)` runs the command and pastes its output into the surrounding line — that is how today's date lands in the filename.

hints.title: Quotes matter
hints.content: Put quotes around the path but NOT around the substitution: `tar -czf "/tmp/backups/etc-$(date +%F).tar.gz"` — quoted '$(date)' would stay literal text.

hints.title: Verify the name
hints.content: `ls /tmp/backups/` must show etc-2026-06-17-style naming matching TODAY's date.

acceptance_criteria.description: etc-<today>.tar.gz exists in /tmp/backups (name matches today's date)
the backup is a valid gzipped archive
